How long does it take to drive around Koh Samui? | About 90 minutes non-stop on the 51 km ring road (Route 4169), or a full day with stops. From Chaweng, every sight on the island is within about 45 minutes by car or scooter in dry weather.
Which part of Koh Samui is best to visit? | For a first visit, base yourself in Chaweng or Bophut and spend days in the south (Hin Ta and Hin Yai, Na Muang, Thong Krut for Pig Island) and one evening on the west coast for the sunset. Choeng Mon suits families with small children; Lamai and Maenam are better value and quieter.
What are the must-see places on Koh Samui? | The Big Buddha and Wat Plai Laem in the north-east, Fisherman's Village on a Friday night, Hin Ta and Hin Yai at Lamai, Na Muang Waterfall, the Lad Koh viewpoint, the Red Temple and Guan Yu shrine near Hua Thanon, and a boat day to Pig Island and Koh Tan or Ang Thong Marine Park.
Where is the Big Buddha and is it free? | The Big Buddha (Wat Phra Yai) stands on Koh Fan, a small islet joined by a causeway to Bang Rak on the north-east coast, about 3 km from the airport and 15 minutes from Chaweng. Entry is free (donations welcome) and it is open 07:00–18:30; cover shoulders and knees and take your shoes off on the stairs.
Which beaches on Koh Samui are best for swimming? | Choeng Mon and north Chaweng are the best for easy swimming, and Silver Beach is the best small cove. From October to December the east coast (Chaweng, Lamai) gets big waves and rip currents, so swim only between flags; the north and west coast beaches are calm but shallow, so swim at high tide.
Where do Pig Island boats leave from? | From Thong Krut pier on the south-west coast, about 40 minutes by road from Chaweng. Pig Island (Koh Madsum) is 15–30 minutes by boat from there; our shared speedboat tour includes minibus pickup from most areas of Koh Samui.
What should I wear to visit temples on Koh Samui? | Cover your shoulders and knees (a sarong or light trousers work), take your shoes off before entering any building and don't point your feet at a Buddha image. The same applies at Wat Khunaram, where the mummified monk sits in a glass case.
Are Koh Samui's waterfalls worth visiting in the dry season? | Less so: Na Muang 1 and 2 shrink to a trickle from February to April, so go in the morning and treat them as a short stop on a south-coast day rather than the main event. The falls are fullest from October to January, when the trails are also muddiest and slippery.
